clue.text: Whitman, perhaps, capturing English hotel's opulence

indicators.note: capturing says the poet's name takes the next letter into itself

parts.note: Walt Whitman, the American poet; 'perhaps' marks his first name as one example of WALT
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American poet staying at a lavish English hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whitman, perhaps' is not the poet's surname but a pointer to his first name, Walt.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence and wealth are both great riches or abundance; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Young man suppressing yen to be a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, pressing it down

parts.note: a lad is a young man
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: A young man holding back his longing in order to become a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as a longing, but here it is the currency abbreviation Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a woman; a plain synonym.

clue.text: A snob set up institute for Japanese art

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A snobbish person founds an institute dedicated to Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like founding the institute, but it turns A SNOB around to give BONSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese craft of growing miniature trees in pots.

clue.text: Like heartless queen's lascivious look

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of the word like are removed, keeping its ends

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A look resembling that of a cruel, heartless queen, full of lust.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, lustful glance at someone.

clue.text: Pain commander inflicted on a revolutionary

parts.note: the head is the person in command
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary, is the usual crossword CHE

explanation.surface: A commander inflicting pain on a revolutionary prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is an ache in the head, a particular kind of pain.

clue.text: Musical elements of play about reaching the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top is the start of the word, so the letter for about climbs there

parts.note: a play is made up of acts
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Parts of a play concerned with climbing to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaching the top' moves C (circa, about) from inside ACTS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running stage musical based on T. S. Eliot's poems.

clue.text: Charms Elvis originally displayed in disastrous GI Blues

indicators.note: displayed in says the first letter of the singer's name appears within the scrambled film title
a disastrous version of the title is a wrecked, jumbled one
originally means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Elvis wins hearts despite starring in the flop film G.I. Blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' scrambles GI BLUES and 'displayed in' puts E, from 'Elvis originally', among those letters. G.I. Blues was a 1960 Elvis Presley film.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile someone is to charm or enchant them.

clue.text: Worm boring around inside swelling

indicators.note: inside says the reversed word sits within the word for swelling

parts.note: a node is a small swelling or lump

indicators.note: around means the word for boring is turned back to front

parts.note: tame means dull or boring

explanation.surface: A worm burrowing into a swollen lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like drilling, as worms do, but means dull; 'around' and 'inside' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A nematode is a roundworm, one of a large group of slender worms.

clue.text: Electronic tag left in coat

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a tag is a label or name

explanation.surface: An electronic tag has been left inside a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy coating, such as a coat of hard paint or the layer on teeth.

clue.text: Beat back section of Royal Fusiliers

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A British regiment's detachment is ordered to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the run YALF, spanning 'Royal Fusiliers', in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to whip or thrash severely, so it can mean beat.

clue.text: Extremely selfish communist has scrap

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme letters, the first and last, of the next word are used

parts.note: a Red is a common nickname for a communist

explanation.surface: A greedy communist owns a scrap of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny strip or fragment, so a scrap.

clue.text: Tart note written by university Romeo

parts.note: so (or sol) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A student Romeo writes a note to a woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' teases with its slang sense of a promiscuous woman; here it means sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart and sour both describe an acidic, sharp taste.

clue.text: Get hint about grabbing husband in horror movie

indicators.note: grabbing says the jumbled letters take the next piece into their midst
about signals the letters being moved around into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone getting a clue about a husband being seized in a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles GET HINT, and 'grabbing' places H among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thing is John Carpenter's 1982 horror film about a shape-shifting alien in Antarctica.

clue.text: Emperor's footman essentially wearing outfit wrong way round

definitions.note: the definition is Emperor; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: wearing says the reversed outfit word is put on around the letter taken from footman
wrong way round means the word for outfit is read backwards

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes, an outfit

indicators.note: essentially means the essential, central letter of the word footman

explanation.surface: An emperor's servant has put on his clothes back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong way round' turns SUIT into TIUS; 'wearing' puts T, the middle letter of 'footman', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor, ruling from AD 79 to 81.

clue.text: Love interrupting elderly relative's lament

indicators.note: interrupting says the letter for love breaks into the relative's name

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an elderly relative
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance cutting into grandmother's grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a deep sound of grief or complaint, so a lament.

clue.text: Keep placing players beside short leg

parts.note: a cast is the set of actors in a play

indicators.note: short means the word leg loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cricket captain sets his fielders next to short leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short leg' is a cricket fielding position close to the batter, but here it gives LE. 'Keep' is a noun: a castle's stronghold tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, and by extension the castle itself.

clue.text: Having captured Troy, oracle castrated bull

indicators.note: having captured says the prophet word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: an oracle is a seer, someone who foretells
T is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights

explanation.surface: A Greek-myth scene: after Troy falls, the oracle's bull is gelded.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy suggests the ancient city, but gives T for troy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young bull that has been castrated and raised for beef.

clue.text: Powder found by detective arresting posh model

indicators.note: arresting says the detective holds the next letter inside

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Cocaine found by a detective who arrests an upmarket fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust is fine powdery matter, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Original couple touring Spain and Germany with daughter

indicators.note: touring says the verb goes around the two country letters

parts.note: to couple is to unite, join together
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A first pair travels around Spain and Germany with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a noun but is the verb UNITE, which goes round E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: An unedited text is in its original form, not changed by an editor.

clue.text: Endless nonsense is eschewed by all?

definitions.note: someone shunned by everybody is left on their own; the question mark flags the indirect definition

indicators.note: endless means the word for nonsense loses its first and last letters

parts.note: baloney is nonsense

explanation.surface: Rubbish talk that everyone avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: If everyone shuns you, you end up solitary; the definition describes a state rather than giving a synonym.

clue.text: Haughty king stops upcoming artist performing tango

indicators.note: stops says the king letter plugs a gap in the following letters
upcoming in a down clue means read from the bottom up

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: performing means the letters of tango are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king halts a rising artist dancing the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; 'upcoming', 'performing' and 'stops' are the three indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty and arrogant both describe someone proud and disdainful.

clue.text: Starts to extol Ambassador Suite, emphasising comfort

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A hotel brochure praising its Ambassador Suite for comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from discomfort, so a synonym of comfort.

clue.text: Inspector's son kidnapped by hideous crone

definitions.note: the definition is Inspector; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: kidnapped by says the letter for son is held inside the other letters
hideous suggests the letters of crone are twisted into an ugly new form

explanation.surface: A police inspector's son has been abducted by an ugly old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hideous' scrambles CRONE and 'kidnapped by' holds S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor inspects books, films or letters and cuts objectionable material.

clue.text: Article about holidaymaker spurning old stripper

indicators.note: about means the article is turned round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: spurning says the letter for old is rejected from the holidaymaker word

parts.note: a tourist is someone on holiday

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a tourist who turned down an aged exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN into NA; 'spurning old' removes O from TOURIST. 'stripper' is someone who strips off, not a dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is a nudist, someone who strips off their clothes.

clue.text: Lowlife got over being given time inside

indicators.note: inside says the time word is placed within the reversed letters
over means the word got is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A criminal reformed after serving time in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is used as written and turned 'over'. TOERAG is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toerag is a worthless, despicable person, so a lowlife.

clue.text: Left welcomes new support

indicators.note: welcomes says the word for left takes the next letter inside

parts.note: split is slang for left, departed

explanation.surface: The political left embraces a fresh supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the side or the political left, but means departed: SPLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip that supports a broken bone.

clue.text: Weapon's power deployed by Eisenhower

definitions.note: the definition is Weapon; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight D. Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A weapon's power unleashed by General Eisenhower.
explanation.definitionFit: A pike is a long infantry spear, a weapon.

clue.text: Noble prematurely abandoning leader of Yorkists

indicators.note: abandoning says the letter that follows is dropped from the word for prematurely

parts.note: early means before the expected time, prematurely

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of Yorkists

explanation.surface: A nobleman deserting the Yorkist leader too soon, Wars of the Roses style.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking below a marquess.

clue.text: Covert resistance fostered by Tory minister

indicators.note: fostered by says the letter is taken in by the minister's name

parts.note: Michael Gove, a long-serving Conservative cabinet minister
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A secret resistance movement backed by a Conservative minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covert' reads as secret, but here it is a noun: a thicket sheltering game.
explanation.definitionFit: A covert is a thicket where game hides; a grove is a small wood, so the two overlap.

clue.text: Read Orwell's letters regularly; they epitomise wisdom

indicators.note: taking the letters regularly means every other letter of Orwell's is used

explanation.surface: Studying alternate letters in George Orwell's writing as a source of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are the traditional symbol of wisdom, as with Athena's owl.

clue.text: Beginning to engrave lines on bishop's ring

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the bishop letter comes first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An engraver starting to cut lines into a bishop's ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is a bishop's jewelled ring in the surface but a verb or noun for chiming in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell rings, and a ring is a telephone call or chime, as in 'give me a bell'.

clue.text: Outlaw ultimately overcame nemesis

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An outlaw finally defeats his arch-enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bane is the cause of someone's ruin or misery, much like a nemesis.

clue.text: Nationalists collecting money for intelligence cell?

indicators.note: collecting says the two letters gather the currency between them

parts.note: N is short for nationalist, so NN is the plural
the euro is a currency, a form of money

explanation.surface: Nationalist groups fundraising for a spy cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence cell' suggests espionage; the question mark flags a brain cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the brain and so of intelligence.

clue.text: Right admitted to bias in education

indicators.note: admitted to says the letter for right is let into the word for bias

parts.note: a leaning is a bias or inclination

explanation.surface: Someone conceding there is a right-wing bias in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the knowledge gained through study, much like education.
